item.text: The Corruption and Crime Commission commissioned an independent survey of 380 WA adults about the Commission and the public sector.
item.support: commissioned an independent research survey of 380 Western Australians.

item.text: The Commission reported high public awareness and confidence in its complaint investigations, alongside broad support for its independence.
item.support: Confidence was equally high with 8 in 10 respondents confident that the Commission would properly investigate their complaints.

item.text: It also reported public concern about the detection of misconduct and possible consequences for people who complain.
item.support: 5 in 10 respondents believing that the chances of detecting misconduct were slim

item.text: The Commission cautioned that the results indicated possible issues and did not provide definitive answers.
item.support: Results should largely be considered as indicative of possible issues rather as providing definitive answers.

item.text: It identified understanding of its role, confidence in complaints processes and expectations about preventing misconduct as areas to address.
item.support: confidence in public sector complaints processes; and beliefs that more can be done to stop misconduct

item.quote: Overall, the survey indicates a generally high level of recognition of and support for the Corruption and Crime Commission by the Western Australian community.
